insights.insight: November 2024 saw a shift in Cabo Delgado from front-line combat to dispersed IS-M strategic maneuvers, with Strategic developments the most numerous event type and only one IS-M IED recorded near Quiterajo on November 25.
insights.context: Intro and ACLED summary for November 2024; IED near Quiterajo on Nov 25; Strategic developments outpaced other event types.

insights.insight: Officials declared IS-M “effectively defeated” with estimated manpower of 200–250 due to foreign-backed gains since 2021, but November data show continued lethal activity and organizational adaptation rather than an end to conflict.
insights.context: Victory narrative versus ACLED November data; references to Rwandan/SAMIM support and reduced large-scale assaults.

insights.insight: Across Cabo Delgado in November, Battles and Violence against civilians each registered 11 high-intensity incidents, indicating persistent lethality alongside increased organizational moves by IS-M.
insights.context: Province-wide event mix showing balance of lethal incidents and strategic developments.

insights.insight: IS-M prioritized positioning, logistics, and signaling in November, as Strategic developments outpaced both clashes and attacks on civilians in IS-M-linked events.
insights.context: IS-M event hierarchy shows emphasis on non-battle strategic activity.

insights.insight: District dynamics diverged: Macomia and Ancuabe were key battle sites, while Muidumbe featured only violence against civilians and no recorded battles.
insights.context: District-level patterns for November 2024.

insights.insight: Clashes concentrated around November 6 and 13–17 in Macomia and the Quiterajo–Cobre axis; late November (25 and 27) saw spikes in Strategic developments, including the Nov 25 Quiterajo IED.
insights.context: Temporal pattern of November events.

insights.insight: The conflict split into two tracks: a narrow corridor of intense fighting (Quiterajo–Cobre) and a diffuse geography of coercive control, looting, abductions, and organizational maneuver elsewhere.
insights.context: Synthesis of spatial-temporal event patterns.

insights.insight: Along the Quiterajo–Cobre corridor, seven IS-M battle events in Macomia over ~10 days caused at least 19 fatalities, confirming it as November’s main kinetic front.
insights.context: Battle clustering and fatality count in Macomia, with a linked clash in Meluco.

insights.insight: Rwandan troops clashed repeatedly with IS-M at Cobre, Mucojo, and near Macomia town, while Mozambican forces engaged IS-M around Quiterajo; Cobre saw three engagements, making it a top battle locality.
insights.context: Force configuration and engagement distribution along the corridor.

insights.insight: Of 12 IS-M battles province-wide in November, seven occurred in Macomia, two in Meluco, and three in Ancuabe; in Ancuabe, IS-M fought local militias rather than formal forces.
insights.context: Distribution of IS-M battles and types of opposing actors by district.

insights.insight: Quiterajo was recaptured by Mozambican forces on November 17, coded as a government regains territory event, but IS-M conducted an IED attack nearby on November 25, demonstrating residual strike capability.
insights.context: Recapture event and subsequent IED near Quiterajo.

insights.insight: Meluco showed rapid insurgent adaptation: battles around November 13 were bracketed by organizational changes, looting/property destruction, and an attack on civilians in Meluco town and Mitepo.
insights.context: Sequence of events in Meluco indicating adjust-and-predate pattern.

insights.insight: Muidumbe recorded eight IS-M events in November, all violence against civilians with no battles or looting/arson flags; six attacks and two abductions resulted in six civilian deaths across multiple localities.
insights.context: Detailed Muidumbe event profile and fatalities.

insights.insight: Macomia and Muidumbe had similar volumes of IS-M events but inverted profiles: Macomia was battle-heavy; Muidumbe was exclusively coercion against civilians, illustrating front line vs. coercive hinterland roles.
insights.context: Comparative district profiles for IS-M activity.

insights.insight: Ancuabe and Meluco mixed battles, strategic changes, and limited violence against civilians; Ancuabe featured abductions without fatalities, and Meluco showed temporal linkage between restructuring and predation.
insights.context: Event mix and co-occurrence patterns in Ancuabe and Meluco.
